items.title: Doncaster Duo Peak Flow Haunt the Headstones in Video for Euphoric Goth Rock Anthem “Never Coming Down”
items.summary: Cross my heart and pray to God Are you the one I’m dreamin of? A racing heart is a notoriously unreliable compass for happiness. It may signal desire, panic—or the… The post Doncaster Duo Peak Flow Haunt the Headstones in Video for Euphoric Goth Rock Anthem “N
items.fullText:
Cross my heart and pray to God
Are you the one I’m dreamin of?

A racing heart is a notoriously unreliable compass for happiness. It may signal desire, panic—or the arrival of someone who can summon both in a single conversation. New love makes a persuasive case for throwing caution aside, though the central nervous system is quick to lodge its objections.

Doncaster, UK duo Peak Flow give that disagreement a considerable charge on Never Coming Down, their new single arriving October 30, 2026. Written by the pair, the track follows the exhilarating early stages of a relationship, when surrender feels irresistible, and self-preservation starts making increasingly urgent suggestions.

Heavy guitars open the song over a throbbing bass groove, while melodic new wave synths introduce a bright, insistent counterpoint to the distortion. The arrangement moves with an easy physical confidence, giving the fuzz enough room to spread without obscuring the hooks. Goth rock, post-punk, and darkwave meet in a chorus built for immediate recall, with the broader guitar wash drawing on shoegaze and alternative rock. Peak Flow call their combination “Anthemwave,” and the name makes sense: even at its most uneasy, the song keeps reaching for a bigger melodic release.

The vocals give that ambition a distinctive character. Somewhere between Placebo’s anxious romanticism and Children on Stun’s gothic theatricality, the delivery makes infatuation sound both intoxicating and precarious. There is enough tension in the voice to complicate the chorus’s upward sweep; every declaration of happiness seems to arrive with its fingers crossed.

The lyrics move from private retreat into the consuming excitement of a new attachment, where a smile seems capable of erasing everything that came before. Yet devotion keeps catching on doubt: the desire to follow someone anywhere sits beside prayers for reassurance and fears of losing control. The repeated promise of staying aloft becomes a plea against another painful collapse.

The black-and-white video places those feelings among gravestones, bare branches, old brickwork, and dim interiors. Outdoor guitar performances alternate with blurred views of trees and figures reduced to silhouettes against the available light. Sunglasses and leather supply the familiar goth vocabulary, while the unstable, smeared images give the setting a more unsettled quality. A cemetery is an appropriately loaded place to declare that you will never come back down, and the contrast between the song’s lift and its surroundings suits a romance already worrying about how it might end.

items.fullText:
Boys Noize has released “Nächstenliebe” featuring Brutalismus 3000, a new single from his upcoming album “7LLVSION,” out November 6 via ONES and ZEROS. The track is built on a step-sequenced bassline in the tradition of EBM pioneers DAF, an act the German producer and his guests cite as a direct influence.

Brutalismus 3000 vocalist Victoria Vassiliki Daldas delivers Dadaist, German-language vocals across a sparse, half-time beat, with a baile funk-styled vocal cutting through the chorus. “7LLVSION” is Boys Noize’s first solo album in five years and follows the single “1+1+1,” made with vocalist ZEP. The album’s full tracklist also features TAICHU, Mayah Alkhateri, ABRA and Safety Trance.

Boys Noize, the project of German-Iraqi producer Alex Ridha, spent the past two years working alongside Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross: he toured with Nine Inch Nails on the “Peel It Back” world tour, co-produced much of the “TRON: Ares” soundtrack, including the Grammy-winning single “As Alive As You Need Me To Be,” and formed the collaborative project Nine Inch Noize with the pair, debuting with a headline Coachella set.

About Boys Noize

Boys Noize is the solo project of Alex Ridha, a German-Iraqi producer, DJ and composer who has written and produced for A$AP Rocky, Bon Iver, Frank Ocean, Arca, Virgil Abloh and Lady Gaga, and remixed Daft Punk, Depeche Mode, Miley Cyrus, Tame Impala, The Chemical Brothers and A.G. Cook. He co-founded the duo Octave Minds with Chilly Gonzales and produces and performs with Skrillex as Dog Blood. Ridha runs the labels Boysnoize Records and the newer ONES and ZEROS, and scored films including “Who Am I” (2014) and Oliver Stone’s “Snowden” (2016).

In 2025 and 2026, Ridha performed alongside Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross throughout Nine Inch Nails’ “Peel It Back” tour and co-produced most of the “TRON: Ares” soundtrack. The collaboration was formalized as Nine Inch Noize, debuting with a headline Coachella set and a same-week studio album. “7LLVSION,” Ridha’s eighth solo album and first in five years, follows that run, with “Nächstenliebe” offering the clearest EBM reference point on the record ahead of its November 6 release.

About Brutalismus 3000

Brutalismus 3000 is the Berlin duo of producer Theo Zeitner and singer Victoria Vassiliki Daldas, who met in 2018 and formed the band in 2020. The pair built an online following during the COVID lockdown period before taking their sound to European club and festival stages, including EDC, Primavera Sound, Coachella, Ultra and Lollapalooza. Their 2023 debut album, “Ultrakunst (Live From Earth),” was followed by the sophomore record “Harmony,” which drew on dubstep, trap, punk, nu-metal and techno. “Nächstenliebe” marks Brutalismus 3000’s feature on Boys Noize’s “7LLVSION.”

items.title: Ironic Sweden release ‘Get It Right (Sophie Rae Remix)’
items.summary: Ironic Sweden have released a Sophie Rae remix of "Get It Right" via Town & Towers Records, pairing the original synthpop track with a club-leaning rework.
items.fullText:
Ironic Sweden have released a new version of ‘Get It Right’, reworked by UK producer and vocalist Sophie Rae, via Town & Towers Records. The synthpop and electropop duo’s “Get It Right (Sophie Rae Remix)” keeps the original’s electronic core while moving the track toward a club-oriented, deep-house-leaning arrangement.

Sophie Rae, credited as an independent producer and vocalist whose work combines electronic production with her own vocal performances, built the remix around new rhythms and layered vocal dynamics. Ironic Sweden described the result as a way to give the song “new life, new meaning and expression.”

“Get It Right (Sophie Rae Remix)” is available to stream on major digital platforms via Town & Towers Records.

Ironic Sweden’s recent single run

Side-Line has tracked Ironic Sweden’s run of singles through Town & Towers Records: the band offered a double single via the label in March 2024 and followed it with ‘Media Whore’ in March 2025. The Sophie Rae remix of “Get It Right” extends that chronology with the act’s first outside remix collaboration documented on Side-Line.

About Ironic Sweden

Ironic Sweden is a Swedish synthpop and electropop act released through Town & Towers Records, the Gentofte, Denmark-based label run by Stig Wintendorff. The band’s Side-Line history begins with a double-single release via the label in March 2024, followed by the single and video “Media Whore” in March 2025.

With “Get It Right (Sophie Rae Remix),” Ironic Sweden hand the song to an outside collaborator for the first time in its documented release history, pairing the group’s electronic songwriting with Sophie Rae’s production and vocal work for a club-focused reinterpretation of the original track.

items.title: WVM shares Halloween anime music video for ‘The Echoing’
items.summary: Los Angeles artist WVM has released a Halloween special anime music video for "The Echoing," mixed by Sean Beavan, pairing the goth single with new visuals.
items.fullText:
Los Angeles solo artist WVM has released a Halloween special anime music video for ‘The Echoing’, out now on YouTube and Instagram. The clip sets the goth-tinged electronic single inside a supernatural, anime-style story for Halloween, with direction by WVM.

“The Echoing” combines ’80s goth influences, electronic textures and blues-influenced guitar in a track WVM wrote and performed on all instruments and vocals. The song was mixed by Sean Beavan and WVM. Beavan has previously worked with Nine Inch Nails and Marilyn Manson, among other acts.

“The Echoing” is also available to stream on Spotify.

WVM’s back catalogue and side projects

WVM is the solo project of a Los Angeles songwriter, multi-instrumentalist and vocalist working across electronic music, alternative rock and cinematic sound. Side-Line covered WVM’s single “Sown” in January 2017, an earlier entry in a catalogue that has grown to include collaborations with Christopher Berg, Sean Beavan, Josh Freese and Chris Vrenna, with music placed in television, trailers and video games.

Outside the catalogue of singles, WVM built Ludwig’s Empire, a browser game centered on the song “Empire” and a mascot character named Ludwig. Players who complete the game receive a code for a free Bandcamp download of that track.

About WVM

WVM is based in Los Angeles and works alone in the studio as a songwriter, multi-instrumentalist and vocalist, writing and performing the material himself before bringing in outside collaborators for mixing and production. The project’s catalogue spans electronic music, alternative rock and cinematic scoring, and Side-Line first covered WVM’s output with the single “Sown” in January 2017.

Since then, WVM’s work has included collaborations with Christopher Berg, Sean Beavan, Josh Freese and Chris Vrenna, and placements in television, trailers and video games. WVM also created Ludwig’s Empire, a browser game tied to the song “Empire.” “The Echoing,” mixed by Beavan and WVM, carries the project’s ’80s goth and electronic influences into a new Halloween-themed music video released this week.

items.title: Paulina Fae releases ethereal wave EP ‘The Way That Only Night Can See’
items.summary: Paulina Fae has released "The Way That Only Night Can See," a four-song ethereal wave EP on Projekt Records, as a name-your-price Bandcamp download.
items.fullText:
Paulina Fae has released ‘The Way That Only Night Can See’, a four-song ethereal wave EP, through Projekt Records. The release arrived October 29 as a name-your-price Bandcamp download, with wider streaming availability following on October 30.

The EP blends atmospheric electronic textures with soft, layered vocals across four tracks. Opener “The Earth Listens” moves through fallen leaves, soil and the steady pulse of the ground beneath the listener’s feet. The remaining three songs, “Flame Lily,” the title track “The Way That Only Night Can See” and closer “Dreaming in Slow Motion,” move through roots, shadows and hidden, unseen places.

Tracklist:

  1. The Earth Listens
  2. Flame Lily
  3. The Way That Only Night Can See
  4. Dreaming in Slow Motion

“The Way That Only Night Can See” is available now as a name-your-price digital download on Bandcamp, with release to other streaming services on October 30.

About Paulina Fae

Paulina Fae makes ethereal wave and dream pop, blending electronic production with soft, atmospheric vocal arrangements. “The Way That Only Night Can See” is her release through Projekt Records, the Philadelphia-based label whose ambient, dark ambient and dream-pop catalog has included Stratosphere’s name-your-price Bandcamp album “Cyclus” and releases from VEiiLA and The Palace of Tears. The EP continues her focus on atmospheric, nature-rooted songwriting set against textured electronic backdrops.

items.title: Pietro Zollo releases two-disc drone album ‘Surface Tension’
items.summary: Pietro Zollo has released "Surface Tension," a 12-track, two-disc minimalist drone album, as a name-your-price download on Projekt Records' Bandcamp.
items.fullText:
Italian composer Pietro Zollo has released ‘Surface Tension’, a twelve-track, two-disc minimalist drone album, through Projekt Records. The album arrived October 29 as a name-your-price Bandcamp download, with wider streaming availability following on October 30.

‘Surface Tension’ moves through slowly evolving drone structures that unfold through repetition and gradual change. Layered drones and synthetic tones form the album’s underlying surface, with piano, viola and woodwinds emerging and receding within it. The full sequence runs close to two hours across two discs.

The album’s two discs build a continuous exploration of tension and release, using the physical phenomenon of surface tension, the cohesive force that holds a droplet of liquid together, as a structural metaphor for shifting inner states. Each track title names one of those states, from the “Static Flow” of the opening disc to the closing “Surface Swell.”

Disc one:

  1. Surface Tension
  2. Static Flow
  3. Surface Echo
  4. Veiled Light
  5. Micro Drift
  6. Subtle Strain

Disc two:

  1. Veiled Reflection
  2. Surface Memory
  3. Surface Fade
  4. Still Current
  5. Glass Skin
  6. Surface Swell

“Surface Tension” is available now as a name-your-price digital download on Bandcamp, with release to other streaming services on October 30.

About Pietro Zollo

Pietro Zollo is an Italian composer who makes minimalist drone, ambient and meditative sound. “Surface Tension” is his release through Projekt Records, the Philadelphia-based label whose ambient and dark ambient roster has included Stratosphere’s name-your-price Bandcamp album “Cyclus” and reissues from Black Tape For A Blue Girl and Lycia. The album continues Zollo’s focus on slowly evolving drone composition, built from layered synthetic tones and acoustic instrumentation including piano, viola and woodwinds, and structured around the physical and psychological readings of tension and release that give the record its title.

items.title: Pan Siateczko releases ‘I Missed Train That Left Before I Was Born’
items.summary: Polish artist Pan Siateczko releases the drone album "I Missed Train That Left Before I Was Born" on Antenna Non Grata, out now on Bandcamp.
items.fullText:
Polish artist Pan Siateczko releases the drone album “I Missed Train That Left Before I Was Born” on the experimental label Antenna Non Grata, out 26 October 2026 as a name-your-price digital download on Bandcamp.

Each of the album’s six tracks takes its title from a small, mildly absurd everyday situation and stretches it into a slow, loud, serious piece of minimalist drone: “A Solemn Funeral For A Houseplant That Received Too Much Enthusiasm,” “A Sneeze At The Auction And The Accidental Purchase Of A Cabbage Oil Painting” and “Standing In Line For Twenty Minutes Only To Find Everyone Is Just Hiding From The Rain” are among the titles. The pieces run from around nine to over fourteen minutes apiece, built from layered oscillators, bass felt as much as heard and long stretches of near-stillness, and the record closes with its first real silence after more than an hour. Pan Siateczko is the recording name of Łukasz Siatkowski, who also works as a visual artist and writer under his own name.

About Pan Siateczko

Pan Siateczko is the music project of Polish artist Łukasz Siatkowski, who also publishes graphic work and writing under his own name. “I Missed Train That Left Before I Was Born” is his latest release on Antenna Non Grata, an experimental label built around minimalist, drone and noise-adjacent work. The album continues the deadpan, slow-built approach to mundane subject matter that runs through the project’s titles, treating small everyday indignities with the same weight and duration as the label’s other dark ambient and drone releases.

items.title: Skycabin release ‘COVET’ EP
items.summary: California duo Skycabin release their five-track "COVET" EP on 28 October 2026, exploring desire, distance and home between Los Angeles and San Francisco.
items.fullText:
Skycabin release their “COVET” EP on 28 October 2026, a five-track record from the California-based duo of Farbod Khoshtinat and Sepand Bahrami that moves through dark pop, trip-hop and industrial-leaning electronics. The EP moves through different shades of wanting: escape, connection, possession, growth and the pull back home.

The title track opens the record with Khoshtinat’s vocal carried over a slow build before distorted guitar breaks into the arrangement; Khoshtinat has described it as the most personal song on the EP, tying together ambition, immigration and the idea of home. “Mirage” follows a relationship that cannot be recovered on its old terms, while “Object of Desire” takes a heavier, industrial-leaning turn that the duo trace partly to Nine Inch Nails. “Midnight Ghost,” released as a single on 30 September 2026 with its own official video, deals with feeling out of step inside one’s own community, riding a dark-house pulse. The closing track, “Hysteria,” puts its lyrics against the collective anxiety the duo observed within the Iranian community during the upheaval of early 2026, and against their own interest in the Dancing Plague of 1518; it ends the EP on fast breakbeats and abrasive synth layers, with no resolved finish.

“COVET” is a return to Skycabin’s core two-person set-up after outside vocalists and musicians featured on earlier releases: Khoshtinat handles vocals, lyrics and arrangement, Bahrami leads instrumentation, composition and mixing, and both share production and songwriting. The duo recorded using a Moog Sub Phatty and a Nord Lead 4 alongside guitar and bass, with percussion built from a Nord Drum 3P and programmed samples; Khoshtinat tracked vocals in Los Angeles while Bahrami built out the instrumentation and mixing in San Francisco, and Christian Wright mastered the EP’s singles at Abbey Road Studios.

About Skycabin

Skycabin is the project of Farbod Khoshtinat, based in Los Angeles, and Sepand Bahrami, based in San Francisco, two musicians originally from Iran who first met in Malaysia around 2013 and spent the following years collaborating before formally founding Skycabin in 2020. Both were part of Iran’s underground music scene, where music was recorded and circulated without official permission. Khoshtinat has also directed music videos for artists including Snoop Dogg, T-Pain and Pitbull, and directed an award-winning short film on Iran’s democracy movement that was screened for the United Nations, the Directors Guild of America and the Motion Picture Association of America; Bahrami works as a sound engineer and producer with more than a decade of studio and film credits. Drawing on Massive Attack, Björk and Radiohead, the duo describe their own sound as a dark pop project with a trip-hop twist. They introduced themselves with the single “Insidia” in January 2023, a song about seduction and identity, and have since built out “COVET” through the advance singles “Object of Desire” and “Midnight Ghost,” released 30 September 2026.

items.title: Feral Business shares Halloween video for ‘Move That Skeleton’
items.summary: Feral Business has released a Halloween video for "Move That Skeleton," an alternative dance-rock track released through the artist's own 1st Drop Music.
items.fullText:
Arizona artist Feral Business has released a Halloween video for “Move That Skeleton”, an alternative dance-rock track issued through the artist’s own label, 1st Drop Music. Feral Business is the project of musician Bear Cole.

The roughly three-and-a-half-minute video sets the song inside a gothic dance party, with a singing skeleton leading a dance army joined by vampires, ghosts, a Wolfman and a krumping gargoyle. “Move That Skeleton” is drawn from Feral Business’s existing catalogue. The Halloween video is the new element. The recording itself is human-made, while the video’s animation was produced in LTX under Cole’s own creative direction.

About Feral Business

Feral Business is the recording project of Arizona musician Bear Cole, released through his own label, 1st Drop Music. The project’s sound sits in alternative dance-rock, and “Move That Skeleton” is a goth-adjacent dancefloor track. The “Move That Skeleton” Halloween video extends the song’s existing catalogue life with a new seasonal visual.

items.title: SKUMLOVE signs to Candlepower Records, covers The Smithereens’ ‘Blood And Roses’
items.summary: SKUMLOVE has signed to Candlepower Records and releases a cover of The Smithereens' "Blood And Roses" on all major digital platforms on October 31.
items.fullText:
Los Angeles industrial and goth band SKUMLOVE has signed to Candlepower Records, a subsidiary of Virgin Music. The signing comes with a new single, a cover of “Blood And Roses” by The Smithereens, arriving on all major digital platforms on October 31.

“Blood And Roses” was written by Pat DiNizio and originally appeared on The Smithereens’ 1986 debut album “Especially for You”. SKUMLOVE frontman and founder Skum Love recorded the cover at Michael Ciravolo’s Saints In LA studio in Sun Valley, with production assistance from Kevin Kipnis. Mastering was handled by Maor Appelbaum in Los Angeles.

Skum Love said the original song had stayed with him for years before he found his own approach to it. “The original song really touched my soul. The struggle between mental health and love plays a big part in many of our lives. Pat DiNizio was truly one of the world’s best songwriters. I knew I wanted to do my own version of this song and it took many years to figure out the ideas that were in my head. I did not want to take away what he created, but add upon it without losing the message. I think we did it justice and opened the song to a new generation.”

About SKUMLOVE

SKUMLOVE began in the Los Angeles underground as an independent project built around Skum Love, starting from homemade recordings and self-released CDs before growing into a nationally touring act. The band has shared stages with Danzig, Type O Negative, Prong, Static-X, Fear Factory, Ministry, Godhead, Spineshank and Combichrist, and its catalogue includes collaborations with Dino Cazares, Burton C. Bell, Tommy Victor, Tony Campos, Mark Gemini Thwaite and Michael Ciravolo.

More than two decades in, SKUMLOVE has continued releasing new material, including the singles “The Dark,” “EGO” and “Ride or Die,” the last of which 16volt remixed. “Blood And Roses” is the band’s first release through Candlepower Records, pairing SKUMLOVE’s industrial and goth sound with a song from outside its own catalogue for the first time under the new deal.

items.title: The Pixel Rain release debut album ‘A Sense of Danger’
items.summary: The Pixel Rain release their debut album "A Sense of Danger" on 29 October 2026 on Bandcamp, an eight-track record led by Aron Siegler.
items.fullText:
The Pixel Rain release their debut album “A Sense of Danger” on 29 October 2026 on Bandcamp. The eight-track record closes out a rollout of advance singles the Southeast London project has run since June, mixing dark electronics, post-punk and synthpop.

The Pixel Rain is led by Aron Siegler, a Hungarian musician based in Southeast London, who combines guitar, electronics and industrial textures with a pop sense of melody, citing The Jesus and Mary Chain and The Horrors among his guitar reference points. The album gathers the four singles released ahead of it, starting with “Last” on 19 June 2026, a track built around authority figures surveying a world of their own making, with a video shot in Hungary. “Glitching Sky” followed on 2 October as the fourth and final advance single, pushing Siegler’s electronic side toward futurepop and synthwave, with Siegler citing VNV Nation and Chvrches as reference points for the track.

‘A Sense of Danger’ tracklist

  1. “Sacrifice”
  2. “Last”
  3. “All The Lovers”
  4. “A Sense Of Danger”
  5. “Danse Macabre”
  6. “Pieces Of Love”
  7. “Glitching Sky”
  8. “All Night Long”

About The Pixel Rain

The Pixel Rain is the project of Aron Siegler, a musician from Hungary now based in Southeast London, who mixes dark electronics and post-punk. The rollout toward “A Sense of Danger” began with “Last” on 19 June 2026, the first track released from the album, followed by “Sacrifice” and the title track “A Sense of Danger” as further advance singles. “Glitching Sky,” released 2 October 2026, closed the advance campaign before the full album’s release on 29 October. The eight-track “A Sense of Danger” is The Pixel Rain’s first full-length release.

items.title: Grove Anemone and DustCats release the album ‘Terroir Unterbreslau’ on Ubocze Rec.
items.summary: Grove Anemone and DustCats release the album "Terroir Unterbreslau" on 30 October 2026 through the Wroclaw netlabel Ubocze Rec., on Bandcamp.
items.fullText:
Grove Anemone and DustCats release the album “Terroir Unterbreslau” on 30 October 2026 through Ubocze Rec., a netlabel based in Wroclaw, Poland. The eight-track record mixes ambient, industrial and drone textures and is available digitally on Bandcamp.

The album is a collaboration between Jakub Sobieralski, who records as Grove Anemone, and Jakub Knoll, who records as DustCats. Its title plays on the German name for Wroclaw, Breslau, and continues the pair’s work exploring the city through sound. In their own description of the record, the two describe a city as a body under strain:

“A city is a vast body. Heavy, bloated, overheated. Made of concrete, glass, badly healed scars, full of splinters and fingernails digging into its skin. After the rain, it sweats rust from cracked gutters, flooding tunnels and garages.”

They extend the image to the people who pass through that body: “Those who belong here and those still learning the names of the stops. Bringing the whole world together, if only for a moment, in a single queue for bread.” The pair describe the record’s sense of place as split between two layers of the same city, “our Besźel and Ul Qoma, two cities stitched together with crooked basting stitches. One shines by day. The other breathes beneath it.”

‘Terroir Unterbreslau’ tracklist

  1. “Szczury”
  2. “Nocny Gaj”
  3. “Pantografy”
  4. “Niemcy w ścianach (strzeż się)”
  5. “Nasyp”
  6. “Fosa”
  7. “Rytuał na skwerku”
  8. “Poniemieckie”

About Grove Anemone and DustCats

Grove Anemone is the recording name of Jakub Sobieralski. Besides “Terroir Unterbreslau,” he has released the albums “Blurring” and “After Hours, No Labels” through Ubocze Rec. DustCats is the recording name of Jakub Knoll, who has previously worked with Hye-gang on the collaborative releases “Tired with all these, for restful death I cry” and, together with Rozmaryn, “Ashes,” both also out on Ubocze Rec.

Ubocze Rec. is a nonprofit netlabel and art collective based in Wroclaw, Poland, that releases music on digital formats, CD, CDr and cassette, and organizes concerts and events in the city alongside its catalogue. “Terroir Unterbreslau” is the pair’s first full collaborative album under both names, arriving as the latest release on a roster that has grown to include acts such as Skutki Uboczne, Sewagesurfers and Giorgio Fazer.

items.title: Sexsomnia release single ‘Subspace’
items.summary: Montreal darkwave trio Sexsomnia released the single "Subspace" on 28 October, the first preview of their upcoming EP "Raven(ous)."
items.fullText:
Montreal darkwave trio Sexsomnia released the single “Subspace” on 28 October, the first preview of the band’s upcoming EP “Raven(ous),” expected in early 2027.

Philip Faith recorded, engineered and mixed the track and wrote its lyrics; Martin Bowes of Attrition mastered it at The Cage Studios in the UK. Faith takes the sole lead vocal, a first for a Sexsomnia single after earlier releases paired his voice with guest vocalists. “Subspace is the Eden of the senses,” Faith said of the track. The single arrived alongside a companion video.

About Sexsomnia

Sexsomnia formed in Montreal, Canada, in October 2021, built around Philip Faith (bass guitars, drum programming, keyboards, vocals) and Pat Gaudette (bass guitars), with Michael K. Rien (electronic percussion, synthesizers) joining soon after. The trio builds its sound on two bass guitars instead of a lead guitar, pairing darkwave electronics and dancefloor rhythms with influences including The Cure, Joy Division, Propaganda and Ladytron. Faith has also worked with Decoded Feedback, Third Realm, Edward Ka-Spel, Oneiroid Psychosis and Blind Agony; Gaudette has played with Unruled, Hexapheen and NowFuture; Rien runs the electronic project Earth Chronicles and was formerly in the nu-metal band Special Ops.

The band’s debut album, “Transcendent,” came out in 2024 through French label Manic Depression Records. In August 2025, Sexsomnia released the “Forbidden” EP, featuring guest vocalists Marita Volodina of Stridulum and Isabelle Young alongside an Attrition remix of “Nigrum Viduam,” with Bowes again handling mastering. “Subspace,” released 28 October 2026, is the first single from the forthcoming “Raven(ous)” EP.

items.title: Leipzig Darkwave Project Kalte Steine Answers the Witches’ Call on “Hexentanz”
items.summary: Zum Hexentanz Das Feuer brennt so heiß Und wir verlieren uns im Kreis Walpurgis Night gives the arrival of May a deliciously disreputable reception. Across Germany’s Harz Mountains, the night… The post Leipzig Darkwave Project Kalte Steine Answers the Witches’
items.fullText:
Zum Hexentanz
Das Feuer brennt so heiß
Und wir verlieren uns im Kreis

Walpurgis Night gives the arrival of May a deliciously disreputable reception. Across Germany’s Harz Mountains, the night of April 30 into May 1 belongs to bonfires, witches, and the prospect of meeting the devil on the Brocken. The season of flowers and fertility arrives with a warning to watch the skies.

Its fires share the calendar with Beltane, the Gaelic festival welcoming summer, when flames also served to protect livestock and ensure good fortune. Six months later, Samhain marks the beginning of winter, its celebrations haunted by returning souls and spirits abroad after dark. Together, these distinct traditions suggest that changing seasons demand more than turning a calendar page: somebody must light a fire, gather the neighbours, and acknowledge whatever might be moving beyond this mortal plane.

Leipzig darkwave project Kalte Steine brings that apprehension into Hexentanz, a German-language single premiering just before All Hallows’ Eve. The song draws on the musician’s childhood near the Harz, where the geography of everyday life comes furnished with some distinctly unusual local residents.

“I grew up in the foothills of the Harz Mountains. There are many old myths and legends surrounding the Harz.”

Among them is the witches’ annual gathering, held at the devil’s invitation. In the account behind the song, they assemble at the Hexentanzplatz, the Witches’ Dance Ground above Thale, circling a fire before flying onward to the Brocken, also known as the Blocksberg. Presiding over proceedings is Watelinde, the head witch named in the lyrics. These stories attach themselves to places people can visit; the region’s Walpurgis celebrations still turn that imagined company into a very public occasion.

The song opens with Low piano notes and storm sounds that set the scene before a cold, melodic guitar figure emerges. Crows caw across the introduction, while the bass supplies a brooding weight beneath the tune. The drum machine moves with the steady insistence of footsteps along a wooded path, giving the arrangement a physical direction. Brief keyboard pulses disturb the spaces between instruments, small electric shivers that make the surrounding quiet feel occupied.

The lyrics follow two companions into the Harz, where mist gathers among firs, and Watelinde welcomes them to the fire. Old songs and spells accompany a dance that accelerates until the light disappears. Morning finds the clearing empty, the flames extinguished, and only a whisper remaining: an assurance that the gathering will return at this time the following year.

The German vocal carries both apprehension and attraction, as though the invitation has already been accepted despite everything its recipient knows. When the chorus arrives, that tension acquires a romantic charge: the repeated title beckons, and the guitar beneath it catches the cold brightness of moonlight through branches. Those recurring synth accents add little pricks of unease without interrupting the melody. Fear and pleasure move at the same pace, each giving the other a reason to continue.

Kalte Steine leaves enough space around these parts for the forest to seem larger than the recording. The piano, birds, and storm establish the setting; the restraint sustains it. By the time the lyrics reach the deserted clearing at dawn, the night has acquired the intimacy of a shared secret, with another arcane meeting already penciled into next year’s calendar.

Listen to Hexentanz below:

Based in Leipzig, Germany, Kalte Steine works across post-punk, darkwave, and synthpop, moving between German and English lyrics. Early singles Shattered, Dysthymia, Wüste aus Beton, and Kinder der Nacht explored isolation, urban estrangement, and nocturnal escape, as discussed in our first feature on the project. Subsequent releases Crying Out, Drowning, and Love Is A Lie extended that vocabulary into social distrust and romantic disappointment. Hexentanz brings those nocturnal instincts back to the folklore of home.

items.title: Dark Minimal Project releases ‘I’m Not in Love’ on Danse Macabre Records
items.summary: French dark electro duo Dark Minimal Project releases "I'm Not in Love," out October 16 on Danse Macabre Records and taken from an album due in 2027.
items.fullText:
French dark electro duo Dark Minimal Project released the single “I’m Not in Love” on October 16, 2026, via Danse Macabre Records. It is the first single from an upcoming album due in 2027.

Guillaume VDR wrote the words and music and handles voices and keyboards; Ange Vesper plays keyboards and pads. Peter Rainman produced the track with Dark Minimal Project and handled mixing and mastering.

“I’m Not in Love” is available now on Bandcamp.

About Dark Minimal Project

Dark Minimal Project is a Lille-based electro darkwave duo formed in 2022 by Guillaume VDR and Ange Vesper. The pair released their debut album, “Cold Black Room,” that year, referencing Depeche Mode’s “Satellite” from “A Broken Frame.” A second album, “Ghost Of Modern Times,” followed in 2023, with arrangement and mixing by Peter Rainman and a tracklist structured as a chronological story between a human and a droid.

The duo’s 2025 album, “Pleasure Is A Sin,” was followed in May 2026 by the EP “And Sometimes,” featuring dBoy of the Paris cold-wave trio Je T’aime on four of its five tracks. Dark Minimal Project has also worked with Front 242, Dominatrix and Das Ich on past remixes.

“I’m Not in Love,” released October 16, 2026 on Danse Macabre Records, is the first single from a new Dark Minimal Project album due in 2027.

items.title: Nena’s ‘Chokmah’ turns 25 on 29 October
items.summary: German singer Nena released “Chokmah” on 29 October 2001 through Eastwest Records. The album turns...
items.fullText:
German singer Nena released “Chokmah” on 29 October 2001 through Eastwest Records. The album turns 25 this year.

Florian Sitzmann produced “Chokmah,” whose title takes its name from the Hebrew word for wisdom. The thirteen-track album runs: “Chokmah,” “Heute hab ich die Sonne mit dem Mond verwechselt,” “Carpe diem,” “Lass die Leinen los,” “Ich hör mir zu,” “Lichtarbeiter,” “Rede lieber nicht zu viel,” “Kann schon sein,” “Silbermond,” “Club der Leisen,” “Du gibst,” “Leuchtturm” and “Dafür ist das Leben zu kurz.”

About Nena

Gabriele Susanne Kerner, known professionally as Nena, began her career fronting the Neue Deutsche Welle band Nena, which took her nickname as its name. The group scored an international hit in 1983 with “99 Luftballons,” propelling the self-titled album onto charts worldwide before the band split in 1987. Nena continued as a solo artist through the late 1980s and 1990s, recording in both German and, briefly, English.

“Chokmah” arrived in 2001 as part of a run of German-language solo albums bridging Nena’s earlier new-wave period and her career resurgence later in the decade, which included a string of greatest-hits and covers collections and a string of German chart-topping albums from the mid-2000s onward. Nena has continued recording and touring in the decades since “Chokmah,” balancing new studio material with revivals of her 1980s catalogue. “Chokmah,” one of the quieter, more introspective records in that run, turns 25 this October.

items.title: Nicolas Balmer shares video for ‘Wand’, from debut album ‘Leben’
items.summary: Zurich multi-instrumentalist Nicolas Balmer shares the video for "Wand," from his debut album "Leben," out December 4, 2026 on Subject To Restrictions Discs.
items.fullText:
Zurich-based multi-instrumentalist Nicolas Balmer has shared the official video for “Wand,” taken from his debut solo album “Leben.” The album is out December 4, 2026, on Subject To Restrictions Discs as a vinyl LP and digital release.

“Leben” moves between New Wave, Kraut, rock and electronics. Raw textures, layered noise structures and an intuitive sense of ambient shape the record, which explores loss and self-discovery, despair, love, guilt and forgiveness.

About Nicolas Balmer

Nicolas Balmer is a Zurich-based multi-instrumentalist, producer and synthesizer enthusiast who has worked in contemporary music for over fifteen years, spanning electronic music, theatre and interdisciplinary projects. His other work includes Nico Sun, the experimental duo Gūsū with Xueyan Chen, and Konstant, his collaborative project with Angelo Repetto.

Konstant released its debut album, “Unbändige Kinder,” on Subject To Restrictions Discs and Default Mode Records in 2024.

“Leben” is Balmer’s solo debut album, due December 4, 2026 on Subject To Restrictions Discs as a vinyl LP and digital release. The lead single and video, “Wand,” introduces the record ahead of its release.

items.title: Derma-Tek signs with Re:Mission Entertainment
items.summary: American industrial project Derma-Tek has signed with Re:Mission Entertainment, with the single "The World Outside" and album "Waiting To Die" to follow.
items.fullText:
Derma-Tek, the electronic and industrial project of Joe Cains, has signed with Re:Mission Entertainment. The label is set to release a new Derma-Tek single, “The World Outside,” followed by the full-length album “Waiting To Die.”

Derma-Tek’s origins go back to the early 2000s, with several demos and compilation appearances preceding the debut album “Corpus Technological,” released in 2006 on DSBP Records and Noitekk Records. A digital companion release, “Defiled,” followed in 2007. New Derma-Tek tracks then appeared sporadically on label compilations before the project went on hiatus.

Cains revived Derma-Tek in 2022. The EP “Looking For Life” came out in 2024 on DSBP Records. Derma-Tek is now on the roster of Re:Mission Entertainment, with “The World Outside” and “Waiting To Die” still to come.

About Derma-Tek

Derma-Tek is the solo electronic and industrial project of American artist Joe Cains, active since the early 2000s. After a run of demos and compilation appearances, Cains released Derma-Tek’s debut album, “Corpus Technological,” in 2006 on DSBP Records and Noitekk Records, with the digital companion release “Defiled” arriving in 2007. Further Derma-Tek tracks surfaced on label compilations in the years after before the project entered a hiatus.

Derma-Tek returned in 2022, leading to the 2024 EP “Looking For Life” on DSBP Records. Derma-Tek has now joined the roster of Re:Mission Entertainment, with the single “The World Outside” and the full-length album “Waiting To Die” announced as upcoming releases.

items.title: Meersein premieres ‘Ruins’ video ahead of October 30 single release
items.summary: German synthpop project Meersein releases the single "Ruins" on October 30, with its music video premiering on Side-Line a day ahead of release.
items.fullText:
German synthpop project Meersein releases the single “Ruins” on October 30, 2026. The track is taken from the upcoming album “Perfection,” whose release date has not yet been announced. The accompanying music video premieres on Side-Line a day ahead of the single’s release.

Meersein is the solo project of Oldenburg-based artist and radio presenter Jan Schütz. “Ruins” explores the consequences of relentless ambition and environmental destruction, built around the recurring line “We pushed too hard, we went too far.” The lyrics describe a civilization in decline: poisoned air, collapsing skyscrapers, burning forests and a sun reduced to a cold, distant observer.

Schütz mixed and mastered the track himself. “Ruins” is released independently as a digital single.

“Ruins” can be pre-saved via DistroKid. The album “Perfection” is available for pre-order through Meersein’s official shop.

About Meersein

Meersein is a solo synthpop and darkwave project run by Oldenburg, Germany-based artist and radio presenter Jan Schütz, blending the sound of 1980s synth music with dark atmospheres and contemporary electronic production.

Side-Line’s coverage of the project dates back to December 2022, when Meersein released its third single, “Speechless”, in an acoustic version. It was followed in April 2023 by “Her Slave”, a single and video featuring post-punk act Corlyx, and in June 2023 by the single and video “Haunting”.

In January 2026, Meersein released “Tide Myself” as the first single and video from the EP “Ocean,” followed in April 2026 by the EP’s second single, “Ariel”. “Ruins” now introduces Meersein’s next chapter, the upcoming album “Perfection,” which explores the boundaries between human ambition, imperfection and the world it creates.

items.title: Depeche Mode’s ‘Speak & Spell’ turns 45 on 29 October
items.summary: Mute Records released Depeche Mode's debut album "Speak & Spell" on 29 October 1981. The Vince Clarke-written synth-pop record turns 45 this year.
items.fullText:
Depeche Mode released their debut album on Mute Records on 29 October 1981, with Sire Records handling the United States release two weeks later. “Speak & Spell” is the only Depeche Mode album made with founding songwriter Vince Clarke, who wrote most of its eleven tracks before leaving the band that December. The synth-pop record turns 45 this year.

Daniel Miller co-produced the album with the band at Blackwing Studios in London, working from an 8-track system that left the songs largely recorded live, with few overdubs. Clarke was the only member interested in the production side, and Miller has said he tried to “capture, as best I could, the atmosphere and the vibes of the songs the way I’d seen them live.” The band had built a following through pub and club shows around Basildon and Rayleigh, Essex, before Miller signed them to his independent label after watching them play a support slot.

“Speak & Spell” runs eleven tracks: “New Life”, “I Sometimes Wish I Was Dead”, “Puppets”, “Boys Say Go!”, “Nodisco”, “What’s Your Name?”, “Photographic”, “Tora! Tora! Tora!”, “Big Muff”, “Any Second Now (Voices)” and “Just Can’t Get Enough”. Martin Gore wrote “Tora! Tora! Tora!” and “Big Muff”, his first two contributions to the band’s catalogue; Clarke wrote the rest. Dave Gahan sang lead throughout. Mute issued three singles ahead of the album: “Dreaming of Me” on 20 February 1981, “New Life” on 13 June, which reached number 11 on the UK singles chart, and “Just Can’t Get Enough” in September, which climbed to number 8 and became a live staple the band kept playing into the 2023-2024 Memento Mori tour. The album itself reached number 10 on the UK Albums Chart.

The original UK pressing, catalogue number STUMM5, included “I Sometimes Wish I Was Dead”; international editions swapped it for “Dreaming of Me”. Brian Griffin photographed the sleeve, a swan wrapped in plastic, and went on to shoot the covers of the band’s next four albums. The record was remastered and reissued in 2006 with bonus tracks, in both standard CD and a deluxe CD/SACD+DVD edition.

Clarke left the band shortly after the Speak & Spell tour ended in December 1981, going on to form Yazoo with Alison Moyet. Gore became the band’s sole writer from “A Broken Frame” onward, released the following year.

About Depeche Mode

Vince Clarke, Andy Fletcher and Martin Gore formed a band called Composition of Sound in Basildon, Essex, in 1980, before Gore saw Dave Gahan play a Moog Prodigy synthesiser at a local pub and recruited him as singer. The four played their first show under the new name, taken from a French fashion magazine, on 14 June 1980. Daniel Miller signed the band to his independent label Mute Records after watching them play, and the synth-pop debut “Speak & Spell” followed in October 1981, with Clarke writing most of it.

Clarke’s departure that December left Gore as the band’s writer for everything after “Speak & Spell”, starting with “A Broken Frame” in 1982. Alan Wilder joined the touring line-up that year and became a full member for “Construction Time Again” in 1983, the album on which the band began sampling industrial sounds with producer Gareth Jones. The Berlin sessions that followed produced “Some Great Reward” in 1984, then “Black Celebration” in 1986, “Music for the Masses” in 1987 and “Violator” in 1990, which carried “Personal Jesus” and “Enjoy the Silence”.

Wilder left in 1995, after “Songs of Faith and Devotion” and its tour. The remaining trio issued “Ultra” in 1997, “Exciter” in 2001, “Playing the Angel” in 2005, “Sounds of the Universe” in 2009, “Delta Machine” in 2013 and “Spirit” in 2017. Fletcher died in May 2022. Gahan and Gore continued as a duo, releasing “Memento Mori” in 2023 and touring it, with the Mexico City shows becoming the concert film “M”. Forty-five years after Mute pressed it, “Speak & Spell” remains the one Depeche Mode album built entirely around Clarke’s songwriting.

items.title: Echo Signal releases single ‘Omen’ on 29 October
items.summary: Minneapolis gothic post-punk band Echo Signal releases the single "Omen" on 29 October 2026, its first new music in seven years and a 2027 album's title track.
items.fullText:
Minneapolis gothic post-punk band Echo Signal releases the single “Omen” on 29 October 2026, its first new music in seven years and the title track of a forthcoming album due in 2027. The single is independently produced and distributed, released through Bandcamp and the band’s own site, echo-signal.com.

“Omen” was recorded at Riverrock Studios in Minneapolis and mastered by Nic Heidt of Respectful Remasters. Echo Signal formed in 2010, founded by Adam Riemenschneider (vocals, rhythm guitar, programming) and Phaedrus Goray (lead guitar) to revisit the genre’s gothic roots in the wake of the post-punk revival. John White plays bass and backing vocals; former member Charles Sadler returned to contribute synthesizer to “Omen” and mixed the single.

Echo Signal marks the release with a show billed as “Harbinger: ‘Omen’ Single Release Show” on 29 October at PILLLAR Forum in Minneapolis, where attendees receive a free digital download of the single.

About Echo Signal

Echo Signal is a dark post-punk band from Minneapolis, Minnesota, formed in 2010 by Adam Riemenschneider (vocals, rhythm guitar) and Phaedrus Goray (lead guitar). The band played its first show in 2014 and released “Demo Tracks” that same year, followed by the EP “Missing” in 2016 and the full-length album “Killer in the Palace” in 2019. Synthesizer duties have passed between several members over the band’s history, including former contributors Rachel Westhoff, Ben Ortega and Charles Sadler; PJ Tracy occasionally joins the band’s live shows on keyboards and synthesizer, and the current lineup programs its drums.

“Omen,” released 29 October 2026, is Echo Signal’s first new single in seven years and the title track of an album due in 2027, with Charles Sadler returning to the fold for the recording and mix.

items.title: Damage Control & OHMelectronic – Red Lines (Digital EP – Metropolis)
items.summary: Following their collaboration with Claus Larsen, Damage Control continues along the same path, this time...
items.fullText:
Following their collaboration with Claus Larsen, Damage Control continues along the same path, this time teaming up with OHMelectronic. I hadn’t heard anything from this project—which involves Chris Peterson, known for his work with Decree, Front Line Assembly, and Delerium—for several years, but I still remembered their music as creative, intelligent Electro.

Preceded by a single, this EP features three tracks. OHMelectronic’s influence is clearly audible, resulting in intelligent EBM with eerie vocals. The music firmly embraces the tradition of Front Line Assembly. Great care has clearly been taken with the sound production, but even more impressive is the attention paid to the actual sound design. The track “Modernity,” in particular, is a real treat and a compelling reason to check out this EP.

This is a top-notch collaboration, and one can only hope that both artists will join forces again to create more music. (Rating:8).

Listen to “Modernity”:

About Damage Control and OHMelectronic

Damage Control is an international electro-industrial collaboration centred on Bill Barsby and Richard Thacker, both originally from Birmingham, England and now based in Australia, together with Alex Wise (Sydney) and Markus App (Germany). Barsby founded the project in Melbourne in 2012 with Thacker and Wise, with App joining soon after. Debut album “Ultranoia” arrived in 2017 on the band’s own Rarefraction Records, mixed and mastered by Chris Peterson with sonic finishing by Greg Reely and guest vocals from Craig Huxtable of OHMelectronic. Side-Line spoke with Barsby about the project in a 2018 Click Interview.

A companion remix set, “Hypernoia The Remixes“, followed in 2020 with reworks by Phil Western, Gin Devo, Tom Slug and Markus App. A new cycle then brought in Leaether Strip’s Claus Larsen as a recurring guest vocalist, producing the singles “Rage” (January 2026) and “Oblivion” (April 2026), gathered on the “Master Of Silence” EP in June 2026 via Metropolis Records.

OHMelectronic is the Vancouver-based project of Chris Peterson and Craig Huxtable (Landscape Body Machine, Noise Unit). The pair started out as Öhm, releasing a self-titled debut album in 2013, before renaming to OHMelectronic for a second self-titled album in 2019 on Artoffact Records, previewed by Side-Line in an exclusive pre-listen and covered in a 2019 Click Interview.

Peterson and Huxtable joined Damage Control for the single “Manifesto” in July 2026, credited as Damage Control & OHMelectronic. “Red Lines”, a three-track digital EP released via Metropolis Records on 11 September 2026 and featuring “Modernity”, continues that collaboration.

items.title: Tomorrows Letters – Shadow Aspect
items.summary: Warm analogue synths, an ’80s vibe and Jungian shadows: discover how Tomorrows Letters are shaping dark wave and synth pop with “Shadow Aspect”.
items.fullText:
Analogue warmth meets the dark side of the soul

Right from the very first listen, the warm, ana­logue synth sound on ‘Shadow Aspect’ by Tomorrows Letters imme­di­ately appealed to me. The Belarusian artist delib­er­ately eschews digit­al ster­il­ity and, using vin­tage hard­ware, real drums and a hand-played bass, cre­ates an organ­ic depth that is rarely found these days. Carried by a mel­an­chol­ic found­a­tion in a meas­ured mid-tempo, a clas­sic 80s synth pop sound unfolds, to which breathy vocal parts lend a fit­tingly sombre dark wave touch.

Theme-wise, the song delves into the deep­er lay­ers of the Jungian psyche. In the lyr­ics, a stranger wanders through his own skin like a ghost in a mir­ror image, until the meta­phor of the shad­ow self becomes tan­gible. An atmo­spher­ic, hand­craf­ted state­ment that com­pletely draws me in.

items.title: “We Bring it Back Again” — Milan’s The Backlash Ride a Wave of 90s-style Psychedelic Shoegaze on “Frame”
items.summary: Everything seems to come and go When the light is gone In the early 90s, alternative rock was enjoying the peculiar experience of becoming the MTV establishment while still dressing… The post “We Bring it Back Again” — Milan’s The Backlash Ride a Wave of 90s-s
items.fullText:
Everything seems to come and go
When the light is gone 

In the early 90s, alternative rock was enjoying the peculiar experience of becoming the MTV establishment while still dressing for a poorly heated rehearsal room. The guitars were enormous, the melodies could reach the back of an arena, and private anxieties were suddenly selling in quantities that required additional warehouse space. Between the Smashing Pumpkins’ lavish distortion and Ride’s buoyant rush, there was plenty of room for a song to stretch its legs and get carried away. Milan’s The Backlash taps into that appetite for that daydream excess on Frame, letting heavy riffs, a rolling bassline, and airy vocals take the scenic route across seven minutes.

Premiering here ahead of its October 30, 2026 release through Elefante REC, the single brings together the heavy guitar attack of Smashing Pumpkins, the rolling momentum of Ride, and a generous helping of Britpop melody. It also offers another look at the Milanese quartet’s forthcoming album, Montage, arriving November 20 through the same label.

The opening guitar figure has the thick, overdriven heft of Cherub Rock, with a bass groove underneath that draws the music toward Ride’s more propulsive territory. That connection becomes clearer in the vocals, whose melodic ease recalls Going Blank Again: the singing gives the ear something to follow as the guitars grow increasingly expansive. There is a distinctly 1993 feel to the combination, particularly in the balance between the riff’s physical weight and the tune’s effortless lift. Over just more than seven minutes, repetition gives the band room to push those elements further, allowing their psychedelic inclinations to stretch out.

The lyrics follow a cycle of disappearance and return, asking to be brought back from a fall and promising to keep calling someone’s name. Light goes away and returns, cold wind disturbs the water, and a bell rings as the singer remains caught inside a frame. The closing repetitions leave him waiting, still reaching toward someone who remains beyond him.

“‘Frame’ is essentially a live recording,” says Francesco Lucà, the band’s guitarist, singer and songwriter. “It lasts about seven minutes, exactly as it is played on stage. The interesting thing is the contrast between what remains when it’s stripped back and what it becomes with the whole band: acoustically, it almost emerges as a psych/melodic song (the band’s internal reference is The Beta Band’s ‘Dry the Rain’), while live it becomes a crescendo of volume, repetition and epicness. The lyrics also lend themselves well to representing this phase: they’re about things that disappear and return, about light going away and being brought back, about still being there, waiting. Without wanting to turn it retrospectively into a song ‘about the band’, it’s hard not to see a certain resonance with the moment the album was born.”

Listen to Frame below, and order the single here.

Alongside Lucà, The Backlash features Alessio Gatto on guitar and vocals, Corrado Carnevali on bass and backing vocals, and Giuseppe Musto on drums. Their discography includes the albums Mindtrap (2018) and Rise (2023). European tours have brought them to Liverpool’s Cavern Club, as well as sharing bills with We Are Scientists, The KVB, and The Academic. Released in collaboration with Flux MGMT, *Montage* follows the singles “Traces” and “Built To Survive.”

Written by Lucà and produced and arranged by the band, “Frame” was recorded and mixed by Lucà at RBS Studios in Milan in 2025, then mastered by James Aparicio. Renée Kohl created the artwork.

items.title: “As Your Mind Dissolves” — Montreal Darkwave Trio SEXSOMNIA Surrender to Sensuality in Video for “Subspace”
items.summary: Crawling out of your skin A silhouette walking in Trapped in silence It’s impossible to see Pleasure can make an unreliable compass. Follow it far enough and pain starts to… The post “As Your Mind Dissolves” — Montreal Darkwave Trio SEXSOMNIA Surrender to Sens
items.fullText:
Crawling out of your skin
A silhouette walking in
Trapped in silence
It’s impossible to see 

Pleasure can make an unreliable compass. Follow it far enough and pain starts to feel inviting, confinement becomes comforting, and the distinction between escape and oblivion grows less certain. Montreal trio SEXSOMNIA examine that uneasy surrender on Subspace, setting the body’s contradictory signals against two bass guitars and a cold electronic beat.

The accompanying video for Subspace unveils SEXSOMNIA’s first new material since their August 2025 EP, Forbidden, offering a tantalizing first glimpse of Raven(ous), their forthcoming EP, due in early 2027.

Subspace opens with eerie synth pads and chilly electronic exhales before a deep synthesizer melody meets the dark, supple movement of post-punk bass guitar. The percussion establishes a steady, insistent pattern, leaving room for the low-end melodies to develop. Around fifty seconds in, additional coldwave textures and feminine moaning samples heighten the sense of anticipation. Nearly a minute passes before Philip Faith makes his entrance, his smoldering gothic delivery lending the words the measured cadence of an incantation.

For all the sampled sensuality surrounding him, Faith takes the sole lead-vocal role for the first time on a SEXSOMNIA single. Earlier releases drew on the contrast between his dark, gravelly register and feminine guest vocals; here, he moves between exposed, vulnerable phrases and a more commanding delivery. Mastered by Martin Bowes of ATTRITION at The Cage Studios, the track gives the band’s dual bass guitars room to carry the melody beneath its atmospheric electronics.

The lyrics describe physical sensation becoming unreliable: skin feels alien, movement gives way to restraint, and pain gradually becomes pleasure. Heat and cold coexist as the body waits for release, while breathlessness and the desire for an embrace draw the speaker further inward. By the closing repetitions, temporary relief has become a wish to remain inside that altered state forever.

Faith explains:

“Subspace is a voyage into the in-between realm of pure, unaltered pleasure, bliss, abandonment and ecstasy; a place where nothing can affect or harm you. But there is a danger in confusing the numbness and perfection of this state with reality. Subspace is the Eden of the senses.”

The video gives that Eden a distinctly biomechanical appearance. Blue-lit figures with metallic-looking skin move among corrugated tubes, their hands passing across faces and bodies in scenes of close, otherworldly intimacy. The Giger-inspired imagery turns physical attraction into something both alluring and faintly threatening, matching the song’s uncertainty about where pleasure ends and confinement begins.

Between these encounters, the band performs through thick haze and saturated magenta, cyan, and white light. Bass players become silhouettes, Faith stretches his arms towards the camera, and close-ups catch the long, pointed metal fingers of his glove. The contrast between the vivid performance footage and the colder, enclosed scenes gives the song’s promises of release an unsettling visual counterpart.

Watch the video for Subspace below:

Founded in Montreal in October 2021 by Philip Faith with Pat Gaudette, and joined soon afterward by Michael K. Rien, SEXSOMNIA put two bass guitars at the melodic center of their music. Their early post-punk and proto-goth foundations meet electronic rhythms and synthesizers, with influences spanning The Cure, Joy Division, Propaganda, Giorgio Moroder, Trentemøller, and Ladytron.

Their debut album, Transcendent, appeared in 2024 through France’s Manic Depression Records. Last year’s Forbidden EP featured guest vocalists Marita Volodina of Poland’s Stridulum and Isabelle Young, alongside an ATTRITION remix.

Listen to Subspace below and order the single here. The forthcoming Raven(ous) EP is expected in early 2027.

items.title: David Bowie’s ‘Stage’ concert experience set for Berlin premiere
items.summary: David Bowie's unseen 1978 concert film becomes "Stage," an immersive arena experience premiering at Berlin's Uber Arena on February 14, 2027.
items.fullText:
English musician David Bowie’s unseen 1978 concert film is becoming “Stage,” an immersive arena experience premiering at Berlin’s Uber Arena on February 14, 2027, in association with the 77th Berlin International Film Festival. Wonderworld is producing the show in collaboration with the David Bowie Estate.

The production reworks 35mm footage that filmmaker David Hemmings shot during three Isolar II tour dates at Earls Court, London, on June 29, June 30 and July 1, 1978, while Bowie was touring behind “Low” and “Heroes”. Bowie was dissatisfied with the results – “I simply didn’t like the way it had been shot,” he said in 2000 – and the film went unreleased. The June 30 and July 1 shows later supplied the official live album “Welcome to the Blackout (Live London ’78),” released by Parlophone in 2018.

Filmmaker Brett Morgen, director of “Moonage Daydream” and “Montage of Heck,” found the Hemmings footage about 10 years ago while researching “Moonage Daydream” and has spent years restoring it for “Stage.” Discussions about an arena presentation began as early as 2018; Rob Hallett, a former AEG Live president of international, joined Wonderworld to lead the production in 2024.

“Stage” combines the restored concert footage with large-format LED screens and a 7.1 surround-sound mix delivered to every seat. Patrick Woodroffe, whose credits include the Rolling Stones and Elton John, designed the lighting; Paul Massey, an Academy Award winner for “Bohemian Rhapsody” and “No Time to Die” who also mixed “Moonage Daydream,” oversees the sound.

The footage shows Bowie’s 1978 touring band: Carlos Alomar on rhythm guitar as music director, Adrian Belew on lead guitar, George Murray on bass, Dennis Davis on drums, Roger Powell on keyboards, Sean Mayes on piano and Simon House on electric violin.

Tickets go on presale October 28, 2026, at 10 a.m. Central European Time, with general sale following October 30 at 10 a.m. CET through Eventim. Wonderworld has outlined further shows after Berlin, including European dates in May 2027 and UK dates – among them a return to Earls Court itself – in June and July 2027, ahead of a wider international run.

“David Bowie has bestowed upon us an extraordinary treasure – an unprecedented concert experience that has yet to be witnessed,” Hallett stated.

About David Bowie

David Bowie (1947-2016) was an English singer-songwriter whose five-decade career spanned glam rock, soul, electronic and art rock, including albums such as “The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars” (1972), “Station to Station” (1976) and “Low” and “Heroes” (both 1977). His 1978 Isolar II tour ran from March to December across North America, Europe, Oceania and Asia, drawing its set from “Low” and “Heroes” alongside revisited “Ziggy Stardust” and “Station to Station” material.

Hemmings’ unreleased film of the Earls Court dates sat in the Bowie archive for almost 50 years before Brett Morgen rediscovered it while researching “Moonage Daydream” (2022), the Grammy-winning documentary built from Bowie’s own archives. “Stage” gives the Earls Court shows their first full concert presentation, following the partial release of the same dates on “Welcome to the Blackout (Live London ’78)” in 2018, and arrives as part of the wider marking of what would have been Bowie’s 80th birthday in January 2027.

items.title: State Alchemist – Ash & Soil
items.summary: State Alchemist’s “Ash & Soil” combines a fat bassline with classic synth pop charm.
items.fullText:
When ash meets earth

What imme­di­ately reminds me of the very finest Swedish synth pop on first listen actu­ally comes, sur­pris­ingly, from the USA. State Alchemist sur­prise me here with beau­ti­ful, rich and won­der­fully undu­lat­ing bass­lines, car­ried by an incred­ibly catchy melody. It reminds me fondly of the sound of the duo ‘Red Cell’. Coupled with har­mo­ni­ous, emotive vocals, the track cap­tures exactly what I love about clas­sic­ally influ­enced synth pop.

The band them­selves describe the song as a story of attrac­tion told through the ele­ments, in which fire, water, ash and earth come togeth­er. When lines such as ‘Ash and soil when you meet me in the eye’ meet this smoul­der­ing sound, built on a subtle groove, I feel pre­cisely that music­al fric­tion born of enthu­si­asm and frus­tra­tion. In any case, I’m abso­lutely delighted to wel­come anoth­er such out­stand­ing track with a genu­ine touch of clas­sic synth pop into my ears.

items.title: Normoria – Jezebel
items.summary: Serpentine, sombre and perfect for October. Normoria’s attempt to combine dark wave and future pop. Does it work?
items.fullText:
A dark seduction in the perfect Halloween guise

The month of October is prac­tic­ally cry­ing out for the per­fect soundtrack, and with ‘Jezebel’, Normoria from Sweden deliv­er just the right dose of dark music for the Halloween sea­son. What imme­di­ately strikes me as a pos­it­ive when listen­ing is that the met­al influ­ence which had crept into their sound in recent years has all but van­ished here, or at least receded so dis­creetly into the back­ground that I’m not shed­ding any tears over it, espe­cially as I nev­er really got much out of those for­ays any­way. Instead, the band quietly bridges the gap between clas­sic dark wave and driv­ing future pop. I’ll delib­er­ately leave it open as to wheth­er this sym­bi­os­is works per­fectly every single second, but I cel­eb­rate the end res­ult as a con­sist­ently strong track.

Lyrically, the band focuses on an ice-cold seductress who, like a cun­ning viper, drives lonely souls mad and drags her vic­tims from the heights of heav­en straight down to hell (with a wink, the lyr­ics are almost in the style of power met­al). My only reser­va­tion con­cerns Angel Moonshine’s vocals. I would have liked a touch more acous­tic under­pin­ning in the mas­ter­ing, even though I much prefer this nat­ur­al pres­ence to over-the-top gimmicks.
